newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch lower, week's rally intact.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch lower, week's rally intact.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly lower Friday, but gains from the week's rally remained largely intact as falling LME stocks, labor concerns and good demand underpinned prices, dealers said.
COMEX's most-active July contract ended 0.20 cent weaker at 116.20 cents per lb, traded 116.40 to 115.40 cents. July finished the week up 4.60 cents.
Spot May ended unchanged at 117.00 cents.
Dealings Friday were sluggish as the market took a breather from Thursday's strong gains when prices settled at their highest in almost a year.
There was also a slight easing in the LME cash to three months backwardation to $78/$83 to dampen the market.
Friday, LME stocks continue to shrink, dipping 2,400 tonnes to 143,675 tonnes Friday.
Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities noted that combined LME and COMEX stocks fell about 13,000 tons this week.
A sharp decline in precious metals also intimidated some, prompting some light profit taking in copper, she added.

U.S. Commerce Department said housing starts -- construction is a key copper consumer -- in April rose 2.6 percent, up from a downwardly revised fall of 7.7 percent in March. Starts in April were at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.473 million, compared to analysts' forecast of 1.43 million.
LME stock falls, possible strikes in Chile's copper sector and good physical demand, especially in the U.S., continued to underpin prices, dealers said.
